notes: Tab slugs and machine scope keys are defined by Foundation ticket 0a and added to this registry there.
purposeKo and roles come from the ui-design.md catalog columns; specs govern details.
flows uses F-codes where the planning document assigns them and end-to-end.md flow names otherwise.
requiresPermission is a gate: the screen and its menu entry are shown only when the role holds roleCodes AND that permission (A01: assistant.use). conditionalGrants never widen or gate visibility.
exampleRoles, conditionalGrants and roleLabelsKo describe planning personas for review only; see permissionModel.

permissionModel.rule: Permissions are actions bound to scope (customer, legal entity, contract, field, period) and are evaluated by the server for the current user and session. Roles are defined per installation in M03 by bundling permissions; the product ships no fixed roles.
permissionModel.exampleRoles: OP/AM/PR/BL/AP/CP/AU/CU/IA are design personas from the planning document and candidate default role templates only. They drive the review preview, never authorization.
permissionModel.visibility: Within the shell of the user's class, a screen and its menu entry are shown when the user holds at least one permission belonging to the screen (its view permission or any of its actions) within the current scope. requiresPermission names an additional gate (A01: assistant.use).
permissionModel.catalog: Foundation 0a defines the permission key naming convention and the permission catalog (view permission per screen object and one key per action), mapping specCommands where specs define them and actionsSummary otherwise. The catalog is a permission contract and needs independent review.
invariants: User class (internal or customer) is fixed per user, set at creation or invitation, never granted by a role; each permission declares allowed user classes; the shell is chosen by user class and visibility applies only inside it.
Separation of duties: catalog declares incompatible permission pairs; multiple roles never lift self-approval limits.
Grant ceiling: users grant or delegate only permissions they hold with a delegable flag within their scope; access administrators do not acquire assigned business permissions.
Sensitive data (amounts, tax, bank details, original or bulk export) are separate permissions from screen view.
